title: Provincial MAID Positions — Mental Illness Expansion

pause_letter.request: Indefinite pause on mental illness MAID expansion

alberta_bill_18.full_name: Safeguards for Last Resort Termination of Life Act
provisions: Limits MAID to Track 1 only (death reasonably foreseeable within 12 months)
Bars MAID where sole condition is mental illness
Prohibits physicians from suggesting MAID to patients (patient must request first)
Prohibits referring patients out-of-province for MAID assessment
Mandates a family member be present during MAID
Creates 150m exclusion zones around refusing facilities
alberta_bill_18.legal_conflict: Directly contradicts 2021 federal amendment that removed reasonably foreseeable death requirement. Legal experts anticipate Charter challenges.

quebec.position: Most expansive — did NOT sign pause letter
quebec.note: Highest MAID rate in the world
quebec.advance_requests: Quebec instructed prosecutors not to pursue charges against doctors who process advance MAID requests — effectively moving ahead of federal law

manitoba.position: Did NOT sign pause letter but has highest denial rate
manitoba.legislation: Explicitly protects regulatory bodies from requiring practitioners to participate

saskatchewan.position: Signed pause letter. No standalone restrictive legislation.
saskatchewan.operates_under: Federal rules via Saskatchewan Health Authority

federal_provincial_conflict.core_tension: MAID eligibility is federal criminal law, but healthcare delivery is provincial jurisdiction
federal_provincial_conflict.alberta_position: Claims Bill 18 does not contravene the Criminal Code
federal_provincial_conflict.legal_expert_view: Charter challenges anticipated if Bill 18 passes
